findings.location: ID-R01 and ID-I01, lines 54 and 60; shared contract lines 7–9
findings.affected_requirement: FR-001, FR-002; Story 18.4 first acceptance criterion
findings.evidence: The shared request carries an 'authenticated operator subject' and an 'authorized owned target reference,' while the contract says unnamed authorities validate them. It does not establish how either host obtains a non-forgeable operator identity, which authority proves an owned database target, or how permission is decided for a standalone Repository. Current IUserContext is Web request oriented; database reachability does not prove ownership. Those are consequential trust decisions for the generator/Web shared port and can be resolved independently of Story 18.1 source grants.
findings.correction_outcome: Define the trusted operator-principal and database-target authorization seams for both hosts, including the standalone Repository case and rejection of caller-substituted identity or target. Identify where authorization is checked before migration/setup and at protected use, then align the shared contract and test seam. Preserve Story 18.1's separate source-grant ownership.

raw_result.summary: REVISE for one independently decidable authorization boundary. Deterministic workflow validation passed. The read-only SpecKit analysis prerequisite reported missing tasks.md, as expected at this mandated pre-task review; post-task coverage analysis remains unavailable. The architecture classification and ID shape are appropriate. Fixed database-per-batch isolation, context provenance, provider binding and ordinary-startup separation align with the accepted October story and architecture. No current Worker Agent tool, Scan strategy or PRD-change planned-change trigger is established. Story 18.1's Repository/root/source identity and contained tool contracts remain unintegrated and unverified; ID-I04 and ID-T04 must be reconciled against its accepted baseline and independently reviewed before tasks or delivery.
